A_RA1_framing_fork.description: DECISION: choose descriptive vs explanatory framing; paper currently 'falls between two stools' (RA.1)

A_RI1_outcome_def.description: DECISION: resolve whether outcome is longevity LEVEL or the Black-White longevity GAP; title/framing/lit review currently inconsistent (RI.1)

A_RA8_multilevel.description: Replace baseline OLS with multilevel models (persons L1, county+D-index L2); fix non-independence and inflated effective N (RA.2.methods)

collateral_risks.risk: Correct effective sample size may weaken significance of the segregation effect, changing core claims
Re-estimated coefficients change the magnitude comparisons to prior longevity studies

A_EiC2_RI6_exclusion.description: Defend exclusion restriction / exogeneity of government-fragmentation instrument; show it is uncorrelated with the health error term (EiC.2 = RI.6)

collateral_risks.risk: If exclusion restriction cannot be defended, the entire causal interpretation collapses to descriptive

A_EiC6_alt_instruments.description: Try alternative identification strategies and instruments per editor (EiC.6)

collateral_risks.risk: Alternative instruments may yield divergent estimates, altering the weight-of-evidence assessment

A_EiC3_residential_selection.description: Address strong selectivity of residential location into segregated counties (EiC.3)

A_RA11_birthFE_interp.description: Resolve the p.18 'experience at birth' assumption; with birth-county FE estimates reflect RECENT not historical exposure (RA.2.methods)

A_EiC5_census_quality.description: Assess problematic nature of matched census data for measuring racial differences across these cohorts (EiC.5)

collateral_risks.risk: Census-match error by race could itself drive the near-identical Black/White age-at-death in Table 2

B_RE1_survivor.description: Address survivor/selection bias from conditioning on survival to 65; engage racial mortality-crossover literature; explain ~0.5yr Black-White age-at-death gap in Table 2 (RE.sample)

collateral_risks.risk: Severe survivor selection may mean 65+ estimates cannot support a longevity claim, forcing a reframing of scope

B_RE3_mechanisms.description: Test mechanisms linking segregation to longevity rather than only reviewing them (RE.mechanisms = EiC.1 causal logic)

collateral_risks.risk: If no proxy mechanism mediates, the explanatory path is not viable and the paper must revert to descriptive
Mechanism results determine whether a DIRECT segregation->longevity effect is defensible

B_RA7_montez_policy.description: Add Montez et al. state-level policy controls (18 domains, 1980s-2005) as moderators/mediators [explanatory path] (RA.1.optionB)

B_RA9_county_controls.description: Expand county-at-death controls (demographic + industrial composition) to rule out spuriousness [descriptive path] (RA.2.methods)

B_RA10_msem.description: Estimate multilevel SEM to combine instrumented + mediating + moderating variables [explanatory path] (RA.3.results)

B_RE6_migration.description: Examine older-age migration: 'returning home to die' and retirement migration to warmer states (RE.migration)

B_EiC7_weight_evidence.description: Assess overall weight of evidence for the observed association (sensitivity / bounding analyses) (EiC.7)

C_RI5_zerosum_def.description: Define 'zero-sum' precisely and derive testable hypotheses; fix p.10 and intro (Quillian 2014) sentences; avoid strawman within-race-homogeneity null (RI.zerosum)

C_RI4_race_moderation.description: Theoretically motivate WHY the segregation->longevity effect is moderated by race (RI.theory)

C_RI3_causal_motivation.description: Strengthen motivation for a DIRECT causal segregation->longevity link vs an effect mediated by violence/income/crime/policy (RI.theory = EiC.1)

C_RI2_gap_literature.description: If outcome is the gap, add literature (section-4 style) explaining differential racial effects (RI.theory)

C_RA3_nonzerosum_case.description: Lay out the non-zero-sum case without picking unnecessary arguments; focus on existing evidence for non-zero-sum Black-White health/mortality differences [descriptive path] (RA.1.optionA)

C_RA4_logan_karbeah.description: Correct characterization of Logan & Parman (2018) and Karbeah & Hacker (2023): neighbor-based measures are MORE granular / less MAUP-prone; real limit is subpopulation focus (RA.1)

C_RA6_proxy_mechanisms.description: Reframe to emphasize mechanisms with empirical proxies (contra p.8 disclaimer); connect to prior work [explanatory path] (RA.1.optionB)

C_RE5_citations.description: Add Williams & Collins (segregation as fundamental cause of health) and Zinzi Bailey review (RE.mechanisms)

C_RE2_lifecourse_nuance.description: Add life-course nuance about the meaning of segregation at 65+ (possibly protective: kin proximity, multigenerational living, reduced loneliness); reconsider 'longevity' scope (RE.lifecourse = EiC.4)

C_RI7_activity_space.description: Reconcile activity-space critique (sec 3.2) with the within-county/between-neighborhood D-index spatial level (RI.methods)

C_RI8_magnitude.description: Move effect-magnitude comparisons vs other longevity studies into lit review and findings, not only discussion (RI.methods)

D_RA2_frontend.description: Tighten/restructure front-end (pp.2-15); cut tangential digressions so front-end maps onto back-end constructs (RA.1)

D_RA5_prune_dynamic.description: Prune 'dynamic environments' / activity-space material (pp.10-11) not tracked by the measure [if explanatory path retained] (RA.1.optionB)

D_RE4_relocate_mechlit.description: Relocate mechanisms lit review to discussion to explain findings rather than set up disappointment [if mechanisms not tested] (RE.mechanisms)

D_capstone_narrative.description: Rewrite intro/discussion/conclusion into one coherent narrative with consistent outcome, defended identification, and settled results (capstone)

E_RA13_typos.description: Fix typos/elisions/repetition: 'full count' p.16, p.4 elisions, 'In the following section' x2 p.8, footnote 5 (RA.4)

E_RI9_p7_copyedits.description: Copyedit page 7 ('Despite notable progress toward...'; awkward Civil Rights sentence) (RI.minor)

E_RI10_white_advantage_claim.description: Fix the false claim that evidence for segregation->White advantage 'remains limited' (e.g., White homeowners benefit from higher prices, sec 3.1) (RI.minor)
